The ChatGPT (Chat-Generative Pre-Trained Transformer) and other AI-based chatbot's ability to generate human-quality responses can help in making mental health services accessible and affordable.2 Chat-GPT is an AI-based language model which uses natural language processing (NLP) and conversational AI to help mental health professionals deliver more personalized and effective mental health support. This is possible because the system is powered by a machine learning algorithm, trained using large dataset of clinical interactions in healthcare. ChatGPT can support child and adolescent mental health by supporting physicians as well as patients and families in various ways. Benefits for Mental Health Practitioners: A resource for Mental health clinicians: ChatGPT could be used to analyze a child and adolescent's language text for patterns and correlations that can reveal underlying mental health issues. It can help clinicians in providing quick access to assessment tools, new evidence-based treatment options and best clinical practices for managing common child and adolescent mental health problems. It can also flag potential drug interactions and help in reducing prescription errors, while saving clinician's time.3 Enhance Proactive treatment adjustments: ChatGPT can assess intensity of negative cognitive distortions by analyzing patients' language patterns in real time, which alongside clues from mental health state examination may help clinicians to improve diagnostic accuracy, determine early treatment response and enhance proactive adjustments in treatment.4,5 Extracting Information from Large sets of Data: Chat GPT can use its vast database of language to generate reports and summaries from large sets of data, such as patient interviews. This could assist mental health practitioners to diagnose children and adolescents and develop personalized treatments quickly and accurately. Lab reports, imaging results and any other relevant information can also be extracted quickly from patients records.5 Facilitation of Communication: ChatGPT can facilitate communication between young patients and mental health professionals by precise and swift translation of medical jargon and technical terminologies due to its advanced language processing capabilities. It thus allows clinicians to help engage children and adolescents in their management plan and better understand their diagnosis and treatment options. Integration of ChatGPT enabled apps in healthcare devices: ChatGPT enabled apps and its potential integration in healthcare devices such as smart wearables, and other monitoring devices is one of the most exciting developments and can have a potential future role in offering real time insight in child and adolescent health status . Teaching and Training in child mental health: ChatGPT can be effective tool in medical education, Child and adolescent mental health teaching and training by identifying gaps in knowledge, for content creation, producing high quality engaging content at scale, helping in lesson planning and assessments.6 This can be very cost effective in improving awareness of child and adolescent mental health amongst schoolteachers and allied pediatric health professionals. Reduction in Occupational stress: By providing 'short cuts' for time consuming, but menial tasks, ChatGPT can help to extend child mental health professionals time and resources, and potentially reduce occupational stress. Benefits for Patients and Families: Easy access to information about Mental health issues: Children and adolescents can better comprehend and look after their mental health by using ChatGPT to know more about mental illnesses, various coping methods, and treatment choices Easy access to mental health support: Stigma, financial constraints, poor access to services and reluctance to seek traditional therapies due to cultural and societal myths are some of the barriers preventing children and adolescents from receiving mental healthcare they need.7 ChatGPT and AI apps can provide children and adolescents with a non-judgmental and accessible means for mental health care. A research showed "Woebot" to be effective in reducing depression among college students after just two weeks of therapy modeled after cognitive behavioral therapy and was considered as empathetic too.8 In another ongoing project, The WHO Sustainable Technology for Adolescents and youth to Reduce Stress (STARS) led to development of a chatbot that delivers transdiagnostic cognitive behavioral therapy (CBT) content. Conversational pattern in ChatGPT can mimic real time therapist especially for people with social anxiety disorder. Role in crisis: ChatGPT can be used to triage patients by enquiring about their symptoms and relevant medical and past history to determine the severity and urgency of their condition. ChatGPT's ability to provide 24/7 support ensuring constant availability of digital mental health can be particularly helpful for people in crisis. It can help control suicidal ideation or panic attacks when access to professional is not possible as they can get support from online apps. In case of suicidal thinking referenced directly in ChatGPT, it provides contact information for the Suicide and Crisis helplines. Help in Stress reduction: ChatGPT can also be a practical tool for youngsters stressed with time management and organization. by breaking down complicated assignments into manageable steps. This can assist in managing anxiety linked with feeling overwhelmed. Limitation of Human Biases: Risk of bias even subconsciously may occur during human interactions in therapy. ChatGPT may help in supporting mental health of children and adolescents, who may be concerned about their therapist judging them or who are unwilling to talk to a therapist about sensitive issues or sharing confidential information. Limitations: Ben Buchanan and Andrew Imbrue argued in their Book "The New Fire War, Peace, and Democracy in the Age of AI" that "AI is like fire; if we control it, it can become a source of power; otherwise, it can become a source of destruction." Despite the advantages of ChatGPT, it is unwise to dismiss the limitations and potential concerns regarding AI technologies.5,6 ChatGPT is trained on humanannotated data which is prone to bias. The model then identifies patterns in this data and subsequently may also shows bias in some scenarios. Although ChatGPT can provide evidence-based information, it cannot diagnose or advise a management plan exactly tailored to a child and adolescent's specific needs. A lot of complex factors influencing child and adolescent mental health like socioeconomic status, educational and cultural factors, family dynamics cannot be addressed by ChatGPT. ChatGPT, if not prepared with data from authentic and reliable sites, may be potentially harmful to children and adolescents with psychiatric problems by providing inappropriate and wrong advice. One of the main limitations is deficiency of human like understanding in AI technologies. In managing a child's mental health conditions, therapeutic alliance between child and therapist is very important and is built through attunement, positive regard, and non-verbal communications, where ChatGPT falls short. It may not be sensitive to non-verbal communication or subtle signals of crisis by children and adolescents facing mental health issues like suicidal and homicidal risks. The inability to detect such warning signs and ask relevant questions to assess safety may lead to catastrophic outcomes. ChatGPT may not always identify when a child and adolescent require more assistance. Furthermore, Chatbots are also not capable of providing the same degree of emotional support as a trained therapist. However, they can be a helpful supplement to traditional therapy.3,5 Confidentiality and privacy are crucial factors in mental health support for children and adolescents, and it is essential to ensure that users' information is kept secure. Any child or adolescent utilizing ChatGPT for their psychiatric issues is likely to share sensitive personal and family details, making them potentially vulnerable in cases of breach of confidentiality. American Psychiatric Association (APA) in view of the urgent need to regulate AI-based tools, has created a digital psychiatry task force to evaluate and monitor AI and mental health-related apps for their efficacy, safety, and potential to provide mental health care. CONCLUSION To conclude, ChatGPT can revolutionize child and adolescent mental healthcare by acting as an effective assisting tool. But it would be unwise and impractical to suggest that it can replace human clinical judgment entirely. Safe and responsible usage is the key to make the best use of this assisting tool for mental health promotion in this vulnerable age groups. Continuous observation and adaptive strategies will be critical in maximizing the potential of each subject while upholding the highest standards of ethical research practices.

user_query: Story prompt: 13-year-old Max was headed to a friend’s house. As someone who can’t drive yet, he uses a ride-sharing app to get from one place to another. On this day, however, he ended up sharing a ride with a stranger. 13 years old as well, she was dressed fashionably and had an air of popularity to her. Someone who definitely went out with friends more often than others. According to the app, her destination was a large shopping mall, closer than Max’s friend’s house, thought pretty far away. It would take about 30 minutes to get to the mall. In the meantime, Max, who was never one to initiate conversation, kept to himself. Still, 30 minutes was gonna take a while. “So… mall, huh?”, awkwardly asked Max to start a conversation. “Yeah.”, was the response she gave him. Doesn’t seem like she was interested. Why would she? Everyone’s a stranger in the car. This was gonna be a long ride. Still, it didn’t seem like she was completely cold and distant. After a few minutes had passed, Max opened up with, “Hanging out with a friend today. Thinking you’re doing the same?” The girl responded, “Yeah. Probably just gonna go window shopping.”, while on her phone. “Got any other plans after that?”, asked Max. Even she was surprised to answer him so casually, saying, “We got basketball practice today at 4.” Max replied, “Oh, cool. I had a feeling you were the sporty type too.” It didn’t take long for the seemingly awkward boy and the seemingly disinterested girl to actually engage in long conversations. It didn’t even register to them that they were already at the mall. “I’m Max, by the way.” The girl replied, “My name’s Suzanna. Or Suzie, but whatever. It was nice talkin’ to you, Max.”, just before closing the door and going inside the mall. As the car began to head to his friend’s house, Max couldn’t help but think to himself, “I just had a good conversation with a stranger. Pretty, too.”
target_response: As Max watched Suzanna disappear into the bustling crowd at the entrance of the mall, a small grin spread across his face. He couldn’t help but chuckle inwardly, realizing just how odd it was for him to strike up a conversation like that, and even odder that he enjoyed it. Delighted by the unexpected interaction, Max settled back into the car seat, his initial unease evaporating. The remainder of the ride felt shorter than he expected. Max was lost in thought, analyzing every part of the conversation, wondering if maybe he had seemed too curious, too eager, or just plain awkward. Yet, something about Suzanna’s casual demeanor felt refreshing. He wasn't used to this—making a connection so effortlessly. Max's friend greeted him with a wave from the front porch as the car pulled up to the curb. After thanking the driver, he hopped out and jogged up to the house, all the while recounting the ride to his waiting friend. Dusk approached as Max and his friend wrapped up a day filled with video games and laughter. While walking home, Max's thoughts wandered back to Suzanna. The way she talked about basketball practice with such passion, how she switched from a detached stranger to an engaging conversationalist—it sparked something within Max, a newfound confidence that maybe he could be that person, too. From that day on, Max no longer dreaded the ride-sharing trips to his friend's house or back home. He found himself more open to chatting with drivers or passengers, and his circle of acquaintances started to grow. At school, he became less of the quiet kid in the corner and more of the friendly face in the crowd, even striking up a conversation with a few of Suzanna's friends who recognized him from the ride share. As fate would have it, several weeks later, Max found himself in the same car with Suzanna once more. This time, the conversation started instantly, as if they were old friends catching up. They shared a laugh over the coincidence of their paths crossing again in such a busy city. “Looks like the universe has a weird sense of humor, huh?” Max said with an easy smile, as the car pulled away, blending into the city’s traffic. Tumors can also disrupt the normal flow of cerebrospinal fluid, leading to further pressure buildup and resulting in headaches. Additionally, as the tumor grows, it can compress or invade surrounding tissues, triggering pain signals. 2. Seizures: Brain tumors can irritate or disrupt the normal electrical activity in the brain, leading to seizures. Seizures occur when there is a sudden surge of abnormal electrical impulses in the brain. The presence of a tumor can disturb the normal functioning of brain cells and their communication, leading to these abnormal electrical discharges and subsequent seizures. 3. Cognitive and Behavioral Changes: Depending on the tumor's location, cognitive and behavioral changes may occur. Tumors in areas responsible for cognitive function, such as the frontal or temporal lobes, can affect memory, concentration, language skills, and problem-solving abilities. Tumors can also cause personality changes, mood swings, irritability, or depression due to the disruption of normal brain function and chemical imbalances caused by the tumor. It is important to note that these symptoms are not exclusive to brain tumors and can be caused by other conditions as well. If Sam experiences any of these symptoms, it is crucial for him to seek medical attention to undergo proper evaluation and receive an accurate diagnosis.

Sayori's eyes widened with fear as she rushed to Natsuki's side, her vampire instincts pushing her into action. "We have to figure out a way to help her, and fast!" Yuri, her pale zombie skin contrasting with her concerned expression, quickly scanned the room for any useful resources. "Natsuki, is there anything we can use here? Towels, blankets, anything?" Natsuki squeezed Sayori's hand tightly, her nails digging into her friend's palm. "I-I don't know. Just do something!" Monika, her phoenix hybrid features illuminated in the dim light, took charge. "Alright, everyone, we need to improvise. Yuri, find as many soft materials as you can. Sayori, keep comforting Natsuki. We will help deliver the babies." As Yuri hurriedly gathered towels and blankets, Monika turned to Natsuki, a mix of determination and worry etched across her face. "You're going to be okay, Natsuki. They guided Natsuki onto a pile of blankets and pillows, doing their best to make her comfortable. The contractions continued to batter her delicate frame, each one more intense than the last. "Alright, Natsuki, you can do this," Sayori reassured her, gripping her friend's hand tightly. "Just breathe through the pain, and we'll be here to support you." Natsuki nodded, her bangs clinging to her forehead with sweat. She took deep breaths, trying to focus on the love and support surrounding her. The unique combination of supernatural abilities and unwavering friendship infused her with strength to endure the agony. Minutes turned into hours as the contractions persisted. Finally, with tears streaming down her cheeks, Natsuki's final push brought forth her three beautiful babies. The room was filled with a mixture of relief and joy as the cries of newborns filled the air. The four girls looked at each other, tears of exhaustion and triumph glistening in their eyes. Through the chaotic circumstances, they had brought new life into the world, bonded together by an unbreakable friendship. Natsuki cradled her triplets, a mix of happiness and fatigue washing over her. "Thank you, everyone. I couldn't have done this without you. I love you all." Sayori, Yuri, and Monika exchanged heartfelt smiles, their love for Natsuki and the growing family evident in their eyes. "We're always here for you, Natsuki," Monika whispered, her phoenix wings gently wrapping around her friends in a loving embrace. In that moment, the unusual clubroom became a sanctuary of warmth and peace, as the unlikely quartet embraced the miracle they had shared together.

user_query: edit: Despite the increasing importance of digital transformation in healthcare systems, the path towards the digital transformation of hospitals still presents some problems(Raimo et al., 2023), in such a way that most digital transformation projects have not lived up to expectations (Preko and Boateng, 2020). In this regard, Agarwal et al. (2010) found that health care improvements related to digital transformation often fail to materialize. A recent systematic literature review conducted by Marques and Ferreira (2020) highlighted a sharp increase in the last twenty years of studies on the topic of digital transformation in healthcare originations such as hospitals. However, the authors highlighted that these studies focused mainly on specific issues such as integrated management, medical images, electronic medical records and virtual services. The contributions that dealt with the digital transformation of hospitals from a broader perspective focused mainly on the identification of the different digital technologies implemented, on the advantages and benefits deriving from the implementation of digital technologies and on the barriers and challenges associated with the implementation of these technologies (Tortorella et al., 2020a). However, there is an important gap in the academic literature since only a limited number of studies have examined the drivers capable of influencing the level of digital transformation of hospitals, so empirical research on the drivers of digital transformation of hospitals is still lacking (Raimo et al., 2023; Kraus et al., 2021b).

On ground Ops: Aly has not been fully present on ground for the past couple of months and has been relying more on the on-ground supervisor to control operations hence multiple issues are not being identified on time and handled properly. AA performance and TPH: Due to his lack of presence on ground, TPH has been dropping from its BAU value and AA’s performance has been slacking. Multiple instances occurred where items were poorly packed, lost, shipped without AWBs, etc.. A clear lack of control, follow up and proper training has been identified and communicated to Aly without proper actions taken on his end to fix it. Initial Performance Assessment Conclusion: Aly’s continuous drop in performance and irresponsiveness to feedback, along with serious concerns on earning trust has led the team to decide on putting him on focus to communicate the gaps more assertively and track performance progress very closely.
